Chapter 729 – Taking Damage.

▸ Status
Axel Highsinger
Race: Tier 0 Human
Resonance: Herald of Ruin
Boon: Multiclass
Bane: ██████████

After a less than ideal first life, Axel wakes as an infant in the back of a caravan.

The world is nothing like his last, brimming with mana, skills, and abyssal invaders. Here, a singular class defines each individual's identity: a swordsman cannot cast spells, and a healer is useless in a fight.

Then Axel opens his status screen for the first time and learns those limits don't apply to him.

While other infants learn to crawl, Axel learns the intricacies of the system. When they take their first steps, he's upgrading his skills. As they form their first words, he's comprehending the essence of mana.

And that's before he starts stacking classes.

The Abyss's influence is spreading, and he'll need all the power he can get if he intends to protect everything he's growing to cherish.

The dust hung thick over the arena floor as the protective barrier shone brightly before slowly fading away. Through the swirling haze, Roland’s sensors pierced the smoke and locked onto the white knight frame. It stood upright near the edge of the crater, its shield still raised, and its front armor plates scorched black but intact. Robert’s voice came through the internal channel, steady, though slightly strained.

“I’m fine. Cockpit seals held. What did you call them… Ah, yes, systems are yellow across the board, but nothing critical.”

Roland exhaled the breath he had been holding. His own overlay confirmed the report. Structural integrity remained high, and the main battery core showed only minor fluctuations. The floating support units drifted back into formation, their energy reserves nearly depleted but still sufficient to keep them operational.

The white frame had not escaped the blast unscathed, however. Several sections of its outer armor were damaged, and Roland could see that some of the runic traces beneath the surface had fractured as well. Robert could still move the frame, but the disrupted flow of mana through those pathways slowed the response of its joints by a fraction of a second. The white knight took a cautious step forward, only for its left knee to lag behind for half a second before catching up.

“I’ll need to repair that before the next match. Gather the dropped mana rifle and whatever battery packs you can recover before leaving.”

Roland relayed the instructions to Robert, who began making his way across the cratered ground. The frame moved awkwardly as its damaged systems struggled to keep up with the pilot’s commands.

Although the damage was not extensive, the results offered valuable data. Developing a way to compensate for the lag caused by battle damage would need to be a priority in Roland’s next revision. With limited time and only one prototype available, he had been unable to thoroughly test how the frame responded to damage under real combat conditions. Simulations could provide useful estimates, but they could never fully replicate the unpredictability of an actual battle.

Robert moved carefully across the broken ground, the white knight’s left leg catching for a brief moment every third step. Its scorched shield hung at its side as its empty sword hand reached down to retrieve the discarded rifle. The black weapon lay half buried beneath ash and shattered stone, its receiver still warm.

As soon as the frame’s fingers closed around it, the magnetic locks engaged with a soft click, securing the rifle against its back. Fortunately, the weapon had survived the blast intact. Several of the battery packs, however, had been mangled beyond use, leaving only two that could be recovered.

Leaving his technology behind for others to examine would be unwise, but there was little Roland could do about the equipment scattered in every direction by the explosion. He would have to settle for what they could salvage.

Across the arena, the Starbloom operator stood frozen beside the command platform. The control rod in his hand had gone dark the moment the core overloaded. His expression shifted from smug satisfaction to utter disbelief as the protective barrier finally dissolved and the roar of the crowd swept through the stands.

The white knight golem was still standing. Its armor was scorched, its movements slightly unsteady, but it remained functional. Unfortunately, there were no rules against unsportsmanlike conduct, and the match was already over. He would rather spend his time repairing the damage than arguing with a bunch of sore losers. That didn’t mean he would simply forget their behaviour, though. He would remember it and make sure to voice his complaints when the right opportunity presented itself.

“The Xandar Institute takes the victory and advances to the best of four! What an explosive finish, gentlemages! Who will they face in the next round, and can they go all the way?”

The announcer’s amplified voice echoed throughout the arena. Cheers erupted from one side of the stands, while a heavy silence settled over the Starbloom supporters. Officials in protective gear hurried onto the field to secure the crater and recover what little remained of the destroyed construct.

Roland paid them no attention. His focus remained fixed on the white knight’s internal readouts as Robert guided the damaged frame toward the exit platform at a normal pace.

Even now, he was analyzing the readings, trying to account for potential future damage while planning the necessary repairs. Although the damage was within acceptable limits, he couldn’t consider the battle a well-fought one. With a better targeting system, they could probably have ended it with a single shot from the rifle. Still, considering how little training Robert had with it, the result wasn’t too bad. If not for the self-destruction tactic and their opponents’ lack of sportsmanship, they would have suffered almost no damage at all.

“Hm?”

He ignored the angry looks from his opponents as he headed back toward the golem hangar, trying to tune out everything around him. However, he soon noticed an incoming communication. When he saw who it was from, he couldn’t help but smile.

It was Lucienne. She had activated one of the calling features he had set up for her. The little spider golem that usually stayed hidden beneath her clothes or inside one of her bags could send him a signal whenever she wanted to contact him. Since long-range communications weren’t a good idea in this place, he needed to get closer before responding. Even so, he already knew what she wanted to ask.

“Don’t worry, Robert is fine and uninjured. The inside of the golem is sturdy.”

Once he was within range, he relayed the message to her bracelet. Meanwhile, Lucienne had told her group that she needed to take care of something first.

“Oh gosh, that was really something! Those people from Starbloom are the worst!”

She replied in an angry tone. It was clear that she held the school in low regard after witnessing such a cheap tactic. Their earlier encounter with the two noble-born mages had only reinforced that impression, and the matter would soon come to a head during the final bout of the treasure hunt.

“Don’t let your anger cloud your judgment. You need to keep a clear head if you want to prevail in the final phase of the treasure hunt. Your team will have to rely on your clairvoyance even more than before, so don’t worry. Robert is fine.”

Lucienne remained silent for a moment before replying.

“I know… I’ll focus on the treasure hunt and make both of you proud!”

“Hah…”

Roland smiled beneath his helmet at his sister’s declaration.

“Once you return, Robert and I will be waiting.”

He wasn’t entirely sure how the schedules would line up, but it was possible that he would finish the golem competition before Lucienne and her team completed the treasure hunt. Both competitions were scheduled to last three days.

After this bout, they would have an entire day before the next one, giving them enough time to repair the damaged plating and runes. The same would apply after the following round, except they would have even longer to make repairs, with the break lasting up to two days. Altogether, the competition would span three days, the same length as the treasure hunt.

Most of the other competitions would wrap up during those three days as well, after which the convocation would finally come to an end.

“I’ll be sure to win! I’ll do my best!”

“Good. That’s the spirit.”

He replied, doing his best to act like a proper older brother, at least for the moment.

“But I think you should get back now. Your friends are probably looking for you, and your event starts in half an hour.”

“Oh, right!”

The communication link went silent, leaving Roland alone with his thoughts as he descended the stairs toward the lower maintenance area. The heavy metal doors of his hangar slid open with a mechanical groan, releasing the smell of scorched mana and heated alloy. Inside, the Runic Mobile Armor stood in the center of the facility, its cockpit open as Robert climbed out.

Robert unbuckled his harness and emerged through the hatch, his boots landing with a heavy thud against the floor. He removed his helmet, revealing sweat-soaked hair clinging to his forehead after enduring the intense mana feedback and heat inside the cramped cockpit. Wiping his face with the back of his sleeve, he turned toward Roland with a weary smile.

“That was closer than I would have liked. The heat from that self-destruct maneuver passed straight through the armor and the mana shield. For a moment, I thought that was it.”

Robert glanced back at the damaged frame.

“Don’t worry. That armor is a lot sturdier than it looks, and the cockpit is reinforced with the best alloys available. It should have been able to withstand even a direct hit from a full core detonation or that lance. Besides, if it detected critical damage, the safety system should have activated the ejection seat.”

Roland explained this with confidence, having spent considerable time designing the golem with the pilot’s safety in mind. If something catastrophic were about to happen, the system could forcibly eject Robert from the cockpit through the rear of the machine, getting him clear of the danger as quickly as possible.

It was obvious that the mages had given little thought to the possibility of the pilot perishing, but Roland could hardly blame them for it. He was the one who had designed a golem intended to be piloted from within, whereas the others relied primarily on conventional golem designs. If something went wrong, the responsibility would fall on him rather than them. Holding a grudge over that would be both unreasonable and counterproductive.

“Glad to know.”

Robert nodded and took a drink of water. Although the battle had been brief, he still looked exhausted.

“You don’t need to worry about the golem for the next day or so, so you’re free to go and watch Lucienne and her event. It’s supposed to last three days, unless they get eliminated early, of course.”

“Hah, that won’t happen. She’s an Arden. She won’t lose.”

Robert laughed, his expression shifting from exhausted to more confident.

“She has the skill and the team to handle whatever challenges they throw at her. Besides, with all the help you’ve given her, the odds are even more in their favor.”

Roland nodded as he made his way toward the workbench, which was lined with tools and spare armor plates. The white knight frame remained kneeling in the center of the hangar, its scorched outer shell still radiating faint heat. He placed a hand against the damaged knee joint and felt the residual mana flow stutter through the fractured pathways.

“True enough. They also have the advantage of having won the last round, which should work in their favor.”

“Oh? Does winning the semifinals give them some kind of advantage?”

“It does. The top three teams are sent to an area with more favorable conditions and fewer construct spawns. They’re also separated from the other teams, which should give them some time to prepare.”

Robert nodded as Roland explained.

“That’s great! A real tactical advantage.”

“It is, but I know you’re probably worried. Go cheer her on, just be wary of your mother. She’ll be somewhere around there as well.”

Robert flinched at the mention of his mother. Although Roland’s relationship with that woman was strained, he didn’t hate her or anything. Too much time had passed for him to keep holding on to grudges over noble squabbles. He had far more important things to worry about, such as expanding his foundation and becoming truly independent of the tier four powerhouses that seemed to be popping up everywhere lately.

“I’ll probably be here fixing the golem, so if anything comes up, just contact me through the usual channel.”

“I will.”

Robert didn’t need to be told twice. He was far more interested in watching Lucienne take part in the treasure hunt than in watching Roland work on the golem. Soon, the area fell quiet as Roland got to work. His armor activated the runes embedded in its surface, allowing him to use magic to lift the metal parts and various tools from the main storage box.

He could use whatever he needed to repair the golem. There were no restrictions on using items stored in spatial spaces, and before the next match, the judges would inspect the golem again. He had barely a day to get everything done, and a considerable amount of metal plating needed to be replaced. The remaining damaged plates would have to be hammered back into shape.

“Time to get to work…”

Although he already had some replacement parts prepared, he didn’t have nearly enough to replace everything that might be damaged. He would have to hammer out the dents first, then determine which parts needed replacing and which could simply be patched up for the time being. Judging by the damage, the golem would probably require at least half a day of hammering and runesmithing.

‘I hope those kids do well…’

Roland got to work while turning on the monitor behind him. Even though he couldn’t be at the arena in person, he could at least listen to the annoying announcer and dedicate one of his multiple minds to keeping track of his sister’s performance. Lucienne didn’t necessarily have to win for his bet to pay off, but after all the training they had received, he would much rather see their team claim victory.

“A round of applause for Xandar’s Institute of Wizardry!”

The moment he switched on the screen, the announcer’s unmistakable voice filled the room, forcing Roland to lower the volume.

This time, the introduction was different. The schools that had qualified for the finals were being announced one by one, with each team entering through a dimensional door as soon as their name was called. This also gave them a slight advantage in terms of timing, as the last team to enter would start nearly ten minutes behind the first.

Ten minutes might not have seemed like much in a competition that lasted three days, but Roland knew better than to underestimate the value of time. Every minute counted, and even a single extra point could make the difference between victory and defeat.

For the moment, he turned his attention to the screen, where his sister had appeared. Lucienne walked into the arena’s staging area alongside her teammates. She looked calm and composed, her posture betraying none of the anxiety that had plagued her during the earlier rounds. One hand rested lightly on the enchanted bracelet Roland had crafted for her.

The other four also looked a bit more confident. Even Elian was strutting forward with his chest puffed out, as though he had already won the final round. Then, out of nowhere, Selphie jabbed a finger into his side, causing the young man to deflate instantly and nearly stumble. The girl shook her head in annoyance, clearly reminding him to stay focused. Oxian and Leron, on the other hand, remained as silent and stoic as ever.

‘They look more like a team now. Camaraderie does tend to form once you’ve been through something together.’

Roland thought about his own past relationships, or rather, the lack of them. He had never been someone who opened up easily to others and tended to prefer doing everything by himself. Still, it was good to share the burden from time to time. Even now, he was working alongside his older brother. Without his help, Roland would probably have ended up with a worse pilot, or perhaps even decided to build a regular golem of some sort, which likely wouldn’t have had much better specifications than the one they had just defeated.

His mana hand spell fished out some plating, and he brought out his portable furnace to melt the damaged pieces down. He had his entire forge stored in his spatial runes for precisely this occasion. First, he needed to straighten out all the dents. Taking the parts off one by one would not be difficult, as he had designed everything with easy removal and repairs in mind.

“There they go! The Xandar team is off! Now, let’s welcome the runners-up, Starbloom Academy!”

As Roland continued his work, the announcer resumed his theatrical commentary, introducing each remaining academy squad with dramatic flair. Roland watched from the corner of his eye as the Starbloom team stepped through their designated dimensional door. Their expressions suggested a mixture of frustration and anger, and it was clear that they were finally going to try to confront his sister this time.

‘So now it starts…’

He watched as the students vanished one by one through the dimensional doors. Various teams appeared on the screen, including his sister’s. They were finally nearing the end. Just one more event, and it would all be over.
